questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to perform zero-downtime upgrades in a CKAD-like scenario with real-world constraints.

## Key Concepts
- Deployment strategy: RollingUpdate with maxUnavailable and maxSurge
- Graceful shutdown via PreStop lifecycle hook
- PodDisruptionBudget to protect minimum availability

## Code Example
```yaml
# Deployment patch focusing on zero-downtime upgrade
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: orders-api
  namespace: prod
spec:
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: "0"
      maxSurge: "1"
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: orders-api
        image: orders-api:1.2
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh","-c","/app/graceful-stop.sh"]
```
```yaml
# PodDisruptionBudget to allow maintenance without dropping below 2 pods
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: orders-api-pdb
  namespace: prod
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: orders-api
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the grace period and ensure no in-flight requests are dropped?
- How would you adapt this pattern for a canary upgrade strategy?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical batch-job composition: init tooling, config-driven scripts, and safe cleanup. 

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes Job TTL, backoff, and completion semantics
- InitContainers alongside main containers
- ConfigMap and Secret mounts; env from Secret
- Resource requests/limits; idempotence

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: db-migrate
  namespace: migrate
spec:
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 600
  backoffLimit: 3
  completions: 1
  parallelism: 1
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache postgresql-client"]
      containers:
        - name: migrate
          image: postgres:15
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: db-creds
          env:
            - name: PGHOST
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-creds
                  key: host
          command: ["psql","-h","$(PGHOST)","-U","$(POSTGRES_USER)","-d","migration_db","-f","/migrate/scripts/migrate.sql"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: migrate-scripts
              mountPath: /migrate/scripts
      volumes:
        - name: migrate-scripts
          configMap:
            name: migrate-scripts
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate idempotence for repeated runs?
- How would you rollback if migration fails after partial progress?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD ability to compose a small, namespace-scoped verification workflow that touches ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, and network policy.

## Key Concepts
- Deployment with InitContainer
- ConfigMap-based allowlist
- Secret-based credentials and TLS sidecar
- PVC-mounted /secrets and lightweight parsing with jq/yq
- Readiness/Liveness probes and per-namespace NetworkPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: compliance-api-creds
  namespace: default
data:
  token: <base64>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: secret-allowlist
  namespace: default
data:
  allowed_keys: |
    tls.key
    tls.crt
    creds
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secret-compliance-checker
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secret-compliance-checker
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache jq curl && wget -O - https://github.com/yq-dev/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/local/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq"]
      containers:
        - name: checker
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "./check.sh"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: secrets
              mountPath: /secrets
      volumes:
        - name: secrets
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: secret-storage
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale and test this in a real cluster?
- What are risks with mounting Secrets in /secrets and how to mitigate?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Security hardening of container runtimes and correctness of patching deployments are critical in real-world CKAD tasks.

## Key Concepts
- SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities drop
- Probes: readiness and liveness on /healthz
- Deployment strategy: RollingUpdate for zero-downtime upgrades
- Validation: load testing, rollout status, and rollback workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: portal
  namespace: secure-app
spec:
  replicas: 2
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: portal
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: portal
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.25
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop:
            - ALL
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
          timeoutSeconds: 2
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
          timeoutSeconds: 2
``` 

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adjust if the app requires a limited capability set?
- How would you implement canary rollouts and monitor for regression?

kind: Deployment
metadata:

      volumes:
        - name: data
          persistentVolumeClaim:

      containers:
        - name: api

            - containerPort: 8080

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical CKAD skills: wiring ConfigMaps and Secrets, configuring InitContainers, implementing TLS sidecars, setting up readiness/liveness probes, and crafting a NetworkPolicy with conditional egress.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMap-driven feature flags
- Secrets for credential management
- InitContainers for tooling installation
- TLS sidecars for secure communication
- Readiness and liveness probe configuration
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: feature-config
data:
  ENABLE_API: "true"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: api-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  token: <base64-encoded-token>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: app-namespace
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: egress-policy
  namespace: app-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: internal-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8080
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
  namespace: app-namespace
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-app
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: installer
          image: curlimages/curl:latest
          command: ['sh', '-c', 'echo Initialized']
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: my-app:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          env:
            - name: ENABLE_API
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: feature-config
                  key: ENABLE_API
            - name: API_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: api-creds
                  key: token
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /status
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /status
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
        - name: tls-sidecar
          image: nginx:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 443
```

## Trade-offs
- **NetworkPolicy complexity**: The policy above allows egress only to the internal-api pod. A more permissive approach might allow DNS resolution but restrict target services.
- **InitContainer overhead**: Installing curl in every pod increases startup time and image size. Consider baking tools into the base image if startup latency is critical.
- **Sidecar maintenance**: A TLS sidecar adds complexity and resource overhead. For simple use cases, TLS could be handled within the application container directly.
- **Secret security**: Storing credentials in a Secret is fine for basic scenarios, but consider external secrets operators or vault integration for production environments requiring rotation.
- **Probe configuration**: Aggressive probe settings can cause unnecessary restarts; conservative settings may delay failure detection. Tune based on application startup time.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: multi-resource coordination, canary rollout, and observability.

## Key Concepts
- Deployments and Services for versioned workloads
- Ingress canary routing and traffic splits
- ConfigMaps and Secrets for feature flags and TLS
- Readiness and Liveness probes
- Resource requests/limits and RBAC basics
- Observability and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```yaml
# Deployment skeletons for stable and canary
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-stable
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: api
        version: stable
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: myrepo/api-gateway:stable
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "128Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "500m"
              memory: "256Mi"
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
```
```yaml
# Canary Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-canary
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: api
        version: canary
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: myrepo/api-gateway:canary
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "128Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "600m"
              memory: "256Mi"
```
```yaml
# Shared Service
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: api
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
```
```yaml
# Ingress with canary rule (nginx-ingress)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: api-ingress
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary: "true"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-by-header: "Canary"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-weight: "20"
spec:
  rules:
  - host: api.example.local
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: api-service
            port:
              number: 80
```
```yaml
# ConfigMap: feature flag
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: api-config
data:
  newFeature: "true"
```
```yaml
# Secret: TLS
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
type: kubernetes.io/tls
metadata:
  name: api-tls
data:
  tls.crt: <base64-cert>
  tls.key: <base64-key>
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical use of ConfigMaps, envFrom, and volume mounting; checks how changes trigger controlled rollouts with an annotation-based restart cue; covers health checks basics.

## Key Concepts
- Deployments, ConfigMaps, envFrom
- Volumes and ConfigMap mounts
- Rolling restarts via PodTemplate annotations
- Readiness and Liveness probes
- Trade-offs: restart cost vs. up-to-date config, ConfigMap size impacts, security

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConfigMap skeleton
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: feature-flags
data:
  FLAG_A: "true"
  FLAG_B: "false"
---
# Deployment skeleton
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: feature-flag-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: feature-flag-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: feature-flag-service
      annotations:
        checksum.feature-flags: "{{ .Values.configMap.checksum }}"
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: feature-flags
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /config/flags
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
      volumes:
      - name: config-volume
        configMap:
          name: feature-flags
```

## Trade-offs Discussion
- **Restart Cost vs. Fresh Config**: Rolling restarts ensure configuration consistency but cause temporary availability reduction
- **ConfigMap Size Impact**: Large ConfigMaps increase annotation length and may affect API server performance
- **Security Considerations**: Environment variables expose config to process inspection; file mounts provide better isolation
- **Update Latency**: Annotation-based restarts are immediate but may be disruptive compared to hot-reload approaches

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical RBAC auditing skills within the CKAD scope, including multi-namespace governance, secure logging, and egress constraints.

## Key Concepts

- **RBAC objects**: RoleBindings, ClusterRoleBindings, and ServiceAccounts at the namespace level
- **ConfigMap-driven policy**: External policy reference for audit rules
- **Namespace-scoped auditing**: Decentralized audit model vs. cluster-wide approaches
- **Pod lifecycle**: InitContainers for tool installation, readiness/liveness probes for reliability
- **Storage**: PVC-backed logging at /logs
- **Network security**: Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting egress to the audit endpoint

## Trade-offs

- **Pros**: Decentralized scaling, namespace isolation, ConfigMap flexibility for policy updates
- **Cons**: Resource overhead per namespace, potential for policy drift, Secret management complexity, duplicated effort across namespaces

## Minimal YAML Skeleton

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: rbac-policy
data:
  policy.yaml: |-
    allowedBindings:
      - kind: User
        name: admin
    maxServiceAccounts: 10
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-credentials
type: Opaque
stringData:
  bearer-token: <token>
  endpoint: https://audit.example.com/api/v1/digest
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: audit-logs
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: rbac-auditor
  namespace: target-ns
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rbac-auditor
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: rbac-auditor
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: busybox
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - "wget -qO /tools/curl https://curl.se/download && wget -qO /tools/jq https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/download/jq-1.7.1/jq-linux64 && chmod +x /tools/*"
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tools
      containers:
        - name: auditor
          image: alpine:latest
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              apk add --no-cache curl jq
              while true; do
                kubectl get rolebindings,clusterrolebindings,serviceaccounts -o json > /logs/snapshot.json
                curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @/logs/snapshot.json $ENDPOINT
                sleep 3600
              done
          env:
            - name: TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: audit-credentials
                  key: bearer-token
            - name: ENDPOINT
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: audit-credentials
                  key: endpoint
          volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: audit-logs
        - name: tools
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit-egress-restrict
  namespace: target-ns
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rbac-auditor
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: audit-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 443
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses familiarity with ConfigMap mounts, InitContainers, and sidecar reload patterns within a single namespace. It also evaluates understanding of signal-based versus in-process reload mechanisms, along with basic security practices using Secrets and NetworkPolicies.

## Key Concepts
- **ConfigMap-driven runtime config**: Externalizing configuration allows updates without rebuilding containers
- **InitContainer provisioning**: Installing tooling (inotify-tools) needed by sidecars or main containers
- **Sidecar watching**: File change detection using inotifywait triggers graceful reloads without container restart
- **Signal-based reloads**: SIGHUP triggers graceful reloads; alternative approaches include local /reload API endpoints
- **Security with Secrets**: Sensitive data like admin credentials should mount via Secrets, not environment variables
- **NetworkPolicy**: Namespace-level egress restrictions limit exposure of internal endpoints

## Trade-offs
- **Signal vs. API reload**: SIGHUP requires the application to handle signals gracefully; /reload APIs add complexity but offer finer control
- **inotifywait vs. polling**: inotifywait is event-driven and efficient but limited to the container filesystem; polling works cross-platform but incurs overhead
- **Sidecar vs. embedded reload**: Sidecars keep concerns separated but add resource overhead; embedding reload logic reduces complexity but couples concerns
- **ConfigMap vs. volume plugins**: Native ConfigMap mounts require pod recreation for updates; external volume plugins enable dynamic updates at the cost of complexity

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical security hardening and runtime verification in CKAD scope, including namespace policies, container security, probes, and network controls.

## Key Concepts
- PodSecurity via namespace labels
- SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities
- Probes: readiness and liveness
- PreStop lifecycle
- ConfigMap mounting and rolling restarts via checksum
- NetworkPolicy egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal patch sketch (Deployment + NetworkPolicy)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: logger
  namespace: logging
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: logger
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: logger
        image: registry.example/logger:1.0
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: cfg
          mountPath: /etc/logger
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /livez
            port: 8080
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]
      volumes:
      - name: cfg
        configMap:
          name: logger-config
```

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: logger-egress
  namespace: logging
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: logger
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 9200
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the rollback path if the ConfigMap causes a regression?
- How would you audit namespace security changes for compliance?
